t: Egyptian, the language of the pharaohs, is with Sumerian one of the two earliest written languages, and its records span more than four thousand years, from the first hieroglyphs to Coptic.
It was written in hieroglyphs, a script of pictures standing for sounds and ideas, and in the faster hieratic and demotic, until the Christian Egyptians adopted the Coptic alphabet, based on Greek.

Forgotten after the last hieroglyphs were carved in 394, the script was deciphered by Jean-François Champollion in 1822 with the help of the Rosetta Stone, reopening the history and literature of ancient Egypt.
dyk: English words such as ebony, oasis and gum come from ancient Egyptian through Greek, and adobe, the sun-dried brick, travelled from Egyptian through Coptic, Arabic and Spanish.
ev: Bone labels in a royal tomb at Abydos carry the earliest known Egyptian writing
A seal of King Peribsen bears the earliest known complete sentence in Egyptian
The Pyramid Texts, the oldest long religious texts in Egyptian, are carved in the pyramid of Unas
The Story of Sinuhe, a classic of Middle Egyptian literature, is composed
A decree of Ptolemy V is inscribed in hieroglyphs, demotic and Greek on the Rosetta Stone
The last known hieroglyphic inscription is carved at the temple of Philae
The last known inscription in demotic is written at Philae
Jean-François Champollion announces the decipherment of hieroglyphs

f.family: Afroasiatic: a branch of its own, distantly related to the Semitic, Berber and Cushitic languages
f.script: Hieroglyphs, with the cursive hieratic and demotic; its last stage, Coptic, in an alphabet based on Greek
f.earliest: Labels from a royal tomb at Abydos, about 3250 BCE; the first complete sentence on a royal seal of about 2700 BCE
f.status: Extinct as a spoken language since about the 17th century; Coptic remains the liturgical language of the Coptic Church
